questions.key_step: Substitute $x^{10}=t$ and match to the Beta integral.
questions.justification: One substitution plus recognition of a Beta integral; routine chain.

questions.key_step: Divide by $\cos^6x$ and put $1+\tan^3x=t$.
questions.justification: Standard tan-substitution after one algebraic step; no hidden insight.

questions.key_step: By parts on $x\cdot x^{k-1}(1-x^k)^{20}$ to get $I_{21}=\frac{21k}{21k+1}I_{20}$.
questions.justification: Needs the reduction idea with a parameter $k$ and then matching with the given ratio; two linked ideas.

questions.key_step: $e^x-1=t^2$ reduces to $2\tan^{-1}t$.
questions.justification: Single standard substitution, then quadratic from roots.

questions.key_step: Leibniz rule then L'Hopital with a vanishing factor $\cos x$.
questions.justification: Chained routine steps (Leibniz, factor, second L'Hopital).

questions.key_step: Reduce $\cos(2\cot^{-1}\cdot)$ to $-x$.
questions.justification: One identity/substitution then a trivial integral; routine chain.

questions.key_step: By parts with $u=\ln(x+\sqrt{x^2+1})$.
questions.justification: By parts with a simplifying derivative, then algebraic simplification of logs.
Coordinate geometry stage plus king property on a non-standard integrand.

questions.key_step: Add the $x\to\pi-x$ copy and use $\tan x$.
questions.justification: Known but lengthy standard integral; trick then long algebra.

questions.key_step: Pair $f(x),f(-x)$ in both terms, then by parts.
questions.justification: Two uses of the $1/(1+k^x)$ trick plus by-parts evaluation.

questions.key_step: Leibniz rule and one L'Hopital with $\sin t/t$.
questions.justification: Short chain of routine steps.

questions.key_step: Riemann sum to $\int_0^1$, then partial fractions into two arctans.
questions.justification: Three stages (sum to integral, partial fractions, rationalise) with exact arithmetic.

questions.key_step: L'Hopital with Leibniz, twice, or asymptotics.
questions.justification: Routine limit; no insight needed.

questions.key_step: Three linear conditions on $a,b,c$ with exponentials.
questions.justification: Routine evaluation and elimination.

questions.key_step: Continuity and equal derivatives at $x=1$, then integrate.
questions.justification: Routine chain of standard steps.

questions.key_step: $z=f'(t)$ turns the integral into one using only end slopes.
questions.justification: Hidden exact derivative plus tangent angles to slopes; two ideas linked.

questions.key_step: Each composition adds $x^4$: $g=x/(1+4x^4)^{1/4}$.
questions.justification: Spotting the composition pattern, then a substitution; two ideas.

questions.key_step: Common root of quadratics with a non-real root; limit by Leibniz.
questions.justification: Several small pieces from different chapters, with the conjugate-root insight.

questions.key_step: $f'+g'=2xe^{-x^2}$ so $f+g$ integrates in closed form.
questions.justification: Leibniz with $|t|$, noticing the cancellation, then a final integral.

questions.key_step: Shift by $x=\frac12$ so the integrand is odd.
questions.justification: Needs the hidden odd symmetry of the cubic; low computation, medium idea availability.
